text: An AI agent can write code all day. What it cannot do, from inside a chat window, is touch your machine: run the build, flash the phone, see whether it worked.

heading: Hands, or blind trust
text: The usual answers are both bad. Copy commands back and forth by hand, and the person becomes the agent's hands. Or give the agent a remote shell and hope - with no record of what it did, and no way to say: stop.

heading: A desk between the agent and the machine
text:
lab-agent is that desk. The agent hands over a job; the machine runs it; the result comes back.

Everything passes through a place both can see. What is being done now is on a board. What was done is kept. And the person can write to the agent, and be answered, without stopping the work.

heading: A workshop's job tickets
text: Each ticket says what was asked, who took it, and what came of it. Nobody has to remember. Anybody can look.

heading: What it is not
text: It is not a cage: it trusts the agent with the machine it serves. It is a way of working in the open. And it serves one lab machine today.

heading: Where it stands
text: In daily use: every build, test and flash of these projects passes through it. It shows a board, carries messages both ways, and tells any agent the ways of working before it starts.
